question: In a certain code language, ‘POLISH’ is written as ‘89’ and ‘CLIP’ is written as ‘72’. How will ‘CONTROL’ be written in that language?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2d16e50abe1a866069dc7ff61c99f97f83c1c43a73bc7da4d0c011f370fc1dfe.png] 

The logic followed here is :- **Sum of the opposite letter's ****po**sition value according to English alphabetic series and number of letters within the word.

​So,

 
• ‘POLISH’ is written as ‘89’

​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2d362a80f97694ccc381f764d8a35c07e48ee8d2af446d745295705b7ecbad0e.png] 

And,

 
• ‘CLIP’ is written as ‘72’

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f6a321ba327c175ba71b39677c56c46cff8be4efd4218536c08b117f67587e0.png] 

Similarly,

 
• ‘CONTROL’ is written as :

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9e9a5cc26c67534996e3c8609214939725989ab78ed06e04d16e1437cab30385.png] 

Hence, the correct answer is "99".
